title: The Institutes of Vishnu
attributionNote: The code presents itself as the teaching of Vishnu, and its verses are attributed to him throughout. Its actual composition is anonymous, and the surviving text is a compilation of earlier dharmasutra material in metrical form.
description: The Vishnu Smriti is one of the major metrical law books, arranged in a hundred short chapters. It treats the sources of dharma and the conduct of the king, the duties of the four classes and the stages of life, impurity and mourning, the rites for the dead, the law of witnesses and ordeals, and a long series of penances. It is also a ritual handbook: its descriptions of expiatory vows and of the yogic disciplines of the dying are among the most distinctive in the legal literature.
historicalContext: The Vishnu Smriti is later than Manu and draws on the dharmasutras, while its chapter on the self's departure through the veins and the sacred syllables shows the growing influence of yogic and devotional thought on law. Julius Jolly translated it in 1880 as SBE 7, with an introduction and comparative notes.
availabilityNote: Complete. All hundred chapters of Jolly's translation are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per chapter. The volume's title page, contents, introduction and index are not part of the work.
